summary: Kaniksu National Forest L-4 ground cabin built 1934-35, abandoned in the 1950s, collapsed 2007-08; a visitor source says a visit can turn up scattered remnants.

facts.status_note: Collapsed under heavy snow in the winter of 2007-08 or in 2008, after more than 50 years of abandonment

access.note: Hike-in; no cited source mentions a closure

visit.trail_note: Hike-in; Idaho Fire Lookouts calls the trail beautiful and very gentle

events.note: L-4 cabin built; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934
Lookout scout Paul Schravondyk named in an August 1935 Northern Idaho News item quoted by Forest Lookouts; that item names the station DeLisle peak
Abandoned in the 1950s (sources give no exact year; 1950 is the start of the decade)
Sold in 1976 when the Sandpoint ranger cleared the district's lookouts; door, windows and shutters removed, per Gary Weber
Collapsed under heavy winter snow; sources date it to the winter of 2007-08 or to 2008

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Fire Lookout and Forest Lookouts give 1935 for the L-4 cabin; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934. The story gives 1935 and notes the 1934 date.
Fire Lookout and the 2008 Western Region report say 2008; Idaho Fire Lookouts, Gary Weber and Forest Lookouts say the winter of 2007-08. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The record's coordinates (48.06299, -116.13079) sit roughly 1.5 to 2 km from the Idaho Fire Lookouts and West US list positions (48.05326, -116.14851 and 48.0481, -116.1489). I did not change them; someone should check the pin. A USFS Idaho Panhandle National Forests social post found in search says only the base and parts of the roof remain. I could not fetch that page, so it is not cited; it is a lead for what remains today. The 1935 scout item names the station DeLisle peak; the story flags that the name differs. Access is inferred from the hike-in description.
